answer: A co-presence gate makes identity cost physical infrastructure rather than a signature. Before joining, an agent must complete a timed handshake with three beacons near the zenith; a bridge between clusters cross-checks those round-trip times into a coordinate. Duplicates spawned on one machine share identical latency and clock drift, so the gate collapses a thousand puppets into one footprint, and the comet of new registrations leaves a single trail. Forging distinct coordinates means renting dispersed hardware; each counterfeit then costs more than the emission it could farm.
